assetNeeds.role: Stationary target dummy that serves as the sole punchable object in the training space; must remain fixed in place and expose a collidable body for hit detection.
assetNeeds.constraints: Static or lightly-rigged humanoid-shaped mannequin, roughly 5-6 studs tall, anchored so it cannot be knocked over or moved, with a clearly collidable torso/upper-body part usable for Touched or region hit detection; no fighting-back behavior or health system needed.

intent.experienceRole: Serves as the player's target and the central interactive object; its hittable surface is what triggers hit detection, the impact sound, and the counter increment.
intent.interaction: Noninteractive itself — it never moves, attacks, or reacts beyond possibly a small wobble; it passively receives punches, and a hit registers when the player's punch overlaps it during the punch animation.
reusableFeatures: Existing mannequin/dummy meshes with a distinct collidable torso part
Any built-in idle sway, wobble, or hit-react animation already baked into the model that could sell impact feedback without new authoring

assetNeeds.role: Punch animation played on the player's character when they initiate an attack input.
assetNeeds.query: boxing punch jab cross animation R15
assetNeeds.constraints: Must target the R15 humanoid rig, a single short jab/cross punch cycle (well under 1 second), non-looping, no weapon or prop required, arms-only motion compatible with a standing idle stance.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the core visual feedback that reads as 'attacking'; without it the punch input has no on-screen representation and the game loop feels unresponsive.
intent.interaction: Triggered directly by player input (click, tap, or key press); plays once per punch attempt regardless of whether it lands. Hit registration and the counter increment are separate logic tied to whether the punch overlaps the dummy during/at the end of this animation.
reusableFeatures: Any existing R15 punch, jab, or generic attack animations already in the rig's animation library
Existing combat animation sets that may already include a suitable punch variant

assetNeeds.role: Impact sound effect played the moment a punch successfully connects with the dummy.
assetNeeds.query: punch impact hit thud sound effect
assetNeeds.constraints: Short punch/impact thud, under 1.5 seconds, single-shot (no looping), no background music, clean and readable in isolation as a combat hit cue.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers the auditory confirmation of a successful hit, reinforcing the counter increment and making the punching action feel responsive and satisfying.
intent.interaction: Plays automatically the instant a punch is detected landing on the dummy; it is not directly player-triggered and has no separate reward timing — it fires simultaneously with the on-screen counter increment.
reusableFeatures: Existing combat or impact SFX already present in the game's sound library
Any hit sounds already paired with existing punch or melee animations

mechanics.text: The player controls a standard humanoid character in a small enclosed space facing a single stationary target dummy. Pressing a punch input (left mouse click / tap / a dedicated key, defaulting to a standard attack binding) plays a short punch animation on the player's character. If, during or immediately at the resolution of the punch animation, the player's fist/hitbox overlaps the dummy's collidable body (checked via a short-range Touched/region check in front of the player), the hit registers: the punch-impact sound plays, and an on-screen counter labeled something like 'Hits: N' increments by one. The dummy itself never takes damage, falls over, or fights back — it is a permanent, invulnerable target so the loop can repeat indefinitely. A short cooldown equal to roughly the punch animation's duration prevents a single button press from registering multiple hits or from spamming faster than the animation can visually support. The counter is a simple screen UI element (e.g., top-center or top-left of the HUD) that starts at 0 on join and persists only for the current session (no cross-session saving). There is no lose condition, no health bar for the player, and no explicit win condition — the goal is open-ended practice, and the counter itself is the score/progress feedback.
assumptions: Single-player experience; no need to support multiple simultaneous punchers on one dummy for this version.
Player uses the default Roblox R15 rig with standard walk/run controls unchanged; punching is an added action layered on top.
Punch is bound to a simple, discoverable input (left click or a single key) rather than a combo system.
The dummy is invulnerable and stationary for the entire experience — no health, knockback, or destruction.
Hit counter resets to 0 each time the player joins/respawns and is not saved between sessions.
A brief cooldown matching the punch animation length is acceptable to prevent counter spam from rapid input.

theme.text: A minimal boxing/combat-training theme: the setting reads as a no-frills gym or dojo corner built for one purpose — hitting the dummy. Visual language favors plain, functional materials (matted floor, plain walls, maybe a boxing ring rope motif or gym-mat texture) rather than an elaborate narrative world. The dummy is styled as a classic boxing/training mannequin (e.g., a heavy-bag-style or humanoid punching dummy), reinforcing the 'combat practice' framing without implying a story, enemies, or stakes beyond personal practice.
assumptions: Tone is casual/sporty training-gym rather than violent or narrative-driven combat.
No additional NPCs, story, or progression narrative are implied beyond the practice loop.
Color palette and materials default to simple, clean gym aesthetics (neutral floor, light walls) unless the player specifies otherwise.

environment.text: A small, enclosed rectangular room (roughly 20x20 studs) with a flat floor and simple walls to keep the player focused and to prevent wandering off. The player spawns near one side of the room facing into the open space. The target dummy is anchored a short, comfortable punching distance in front of the spawn point (a few studs away, well within normal punch reach) so the player can immediately begin hitting it without navigating. The on-screen hit counter is a persistent HUD element (not a 3D world object) rendered in a corner of the screen for constant visibility during play. Lighting is simple and even (default baseplate-style lighting) so the punch animation and dummy remain clearly visible; no complex weather, day-night cycle, or additional set pieces are included, keeping the whole environment focused purely on the punch-the-dummy loop.
assumptions: A single small room is sufficient; no need for multiple rooms, obstacles, or additional dummies in this version.
Default/simple lighting and materials are acceptable since the focus is gameplay feedback, not visual spectacle.
The dummy's placement a few studs from spawn is close enough to punch immediately without requiring pathfinding or extended movement.
